column5: Species averages, distinct from Atlantic white and western red cedar; not graded lumber or structural design allowables. Specific gravity uses ovendry mass divided by volume at 12% moisture; density = 1000 * 0.31 * 1.12 = 347.2 kg/m3. Bending MOE includes shear deflection at span/depth 14; longitudinal modulus is the source's approximate 10% correction, 1.1 * 5500 = 6050 MPa. MOR is a bending failure index, not uniaxial tensile strength. Compression perpendicular is stress at proportional limit, not ultimate strength. Shear and perpendicular tension average radial and tangential tests. Side hardness is modified-Janka force for half-diameter penetration of an 11.28 mm ball, not pressure. Temperature and per-value uncertainty are unspecified. No moisture/temperature/grade extrapolation, heat capacity, conductivity or loss law is supplied.

column5: Engineering correlations, not additional species measurements or graded-lumber data. Cp in J/(kg K) is 1000*((0.1031+0.003867*T+4.18*0.12)/1.12+12*(-0.06191+0.000236*T-0.000133*12)); its fixed-moisture dependence is affine in absolute T over 280-420 K, so linear interpolation reproduces this model. Transverse conductivity at 297.15 K is G12*(0.1941+0.004064*12)+0.01864 using this bundle's ovendry-mass/volume-at-12-percent G12=0.31. The conductivity correlation requires G12>0.3 and MC<25 percent; the source reports actual conductivity may differ by 20 percent, which is not a statistical confidence interval. No longitudinal conductivity, moisture evolution, drying, phase change, pressure dependence, thermal-density law or temperature extension of the mechanical measurements is supplied.
